div.head: II As 3.1
div.ab: ⁊ se hlaford ðe his ðeowan æt ðyfðe gewita sy, ⁊ hit him on open wurðe, ðolie ðæs ðeowan ⁊ béo his weres scyldig æt frumcyrre; gyf he hit oftor dó, béo ealles scyldig ðæs ðe he age.
⁊ se hlaford þe his ðeowan æt þyfþe gewita sy, ⁊ hit him on open wurðe, ðolige ðæs þeowan ⁊ beo his weres scyldig æt frumcyrre; gif he hit oftor dó, beo he ealles scyldig þæs he age.

Be ðam hlaford þe his þeowan æt þyfðum gewita sie. Se hlaford þe his þeowan æt þyfðe gewita sie, ⁊ him on open wyrðe, þolie þæs þeowan ⁊ beo his weres scyldig æt fru[m]cyrre; gif he hit oftor dó, beo ealles scyldig þe he age.

De domino qui seruo suo consentaneus sit ad furtum. Dominus, qui seruo suo conscius in furto fuerit et conuincatur inde (conuictus noxe), seruum illum perdat et werę suę reus sit prima uice; si sepius hoc presumat, reus sit omnium que habebit.

[Be ðæm hlaford þe his þeowan æt þyfðum gewita sie.] [So] ⁊ se hlaford þe his ðeowan æt þyfþe gewita sy, ⁊ hit him on open wurðe, ðolige ðæs þeowan ⁊ beo his weres scyldig æt frumcyrre; gif he hit oftor dó, beo he ealles scyldig þæs he age.

And if a lord is accessory to a theft by one of his slaves, and it afterwards becomes known, he shall on the first occasion suffer the loss of his slave and forfeit his wergeld. If he repeats the offence he shall forfeit all that he possesses.

And the lord who is an accessory to theft by his slave, and it becomes known about him, is to forfeit the slave and be liable to his wergild on the first occasion; if he does it more often, he is to be liable to pay all that he owns.

(Von dem Herrn, der Mitwisser seines Sklaven bei Diebstählen ist. So) Und der Herr, welcher Mitwisser seines Sklaven beim Diebstahl ist, und [wenn] es über ihn offenkundig wird, verliere den Sklaven und sei sein Wergeld schuldig beim ersten Male; wenn er es öfter thut, sei er alles schuldig, was er hat.

(Of the lord who is accessory to his slave's thefts. So) And the lord who is accessory to his slave's theft, and [if] it becomes manifest against him, let him lose the slave and be liable for his wergild the first time; if he does it more often, let him be liable for all that he has.
